extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to arXiv (arXiv submitters / researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and step-by-step guidance for deleting, un‑submitting, or withdrawing a submission on arXiv, and the effects of withdrawal on visibility and version history. Covers appropriate reasons, procedure, and alternatives when a submission has already been announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deleting or un‑submitting before announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If your submission has not yet become publicly available you may delete or delay it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From your user page select either the Delete or Unsubmit icon. Deleting a submission will remove it from the system; unsubmitting will return it to the incomplete status allowing modification and later resubmission. If you have difficulty doing either, contact arXiv administrators immediately and include the submission identifier, an explanation of the problem, and the reason for withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot completely remove announced articles; withdrawal creates withdrawn version
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles that have been announced and made public cannot be completely removed. A withdrawal creates a new version of the paper marked as withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new withdrawn version displays the reason for the withdrawal and does not link directly to the full text. Previous versions will still be accessible, including their full text. The submission history will indicate the withdrawn version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to submit a withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit a withdrawal: from your user page select the Withdraw icon for the appropriate article in the 'Articles You Own'. Complete the Withdrawal form by providing a specific reason for the withdrawal within the Comments field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the on‑page Withdraw workflow; ensure you choose the correct article and fill the Comments field with a clear, specific reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal reasons must be appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal reasons must be appropriate for the withdrawal to be accepted and will be displayed publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing the withdrawal reason keep in mind you are explaining the withdrawal to the readers of arXiv. Provide a specific, appropriate rationale in the Comments field; inappropriate or vague reasons may lead to non-acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of inappropriate reasons and suggested alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain reasons are explicitly not appropriate grounds for withdrawal and have prescribed alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not appropriate to withdraw a paper because it is published or submitted to a journal — instead submit a journal-ref. It is not appropriate to withdraw because it is being updated — instead submit a replacement. It is not appropriate to withdraw due to copyright infringement — instead follow the Copyright Infringements procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects on page display, downloads, and version history after withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: The withdrawal creates a new version which becomes the default view of the paper and shows that the paper has been withdrawn and by whom; the reason is displayed in the Comments field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Download options there is no option to download the PDF or TeX for the withdrawn version. All previous versions remain accessible through their version links and their full text can still be accessed under Download options. The submission history will state '(withdrawn)' alongside the new version and a notification banner indicates that a newer version has been withdrawn.
